subject: Pricing follow-up: token volumes & target $/1M (Acme)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T15:02:00Z
Subject: Pricing follow-up: token volumes & target $/1M (Acme)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment: 

Call recap (high level)
- Primary use case: real-time assistant + lightweight summarization for in-app workflows
- Expected steady-state volume: ~100M inference tokens / month (with spikes up to ~150M)
- Embeddings usage: ~10M tokens / month for similarity + vector store refreshes
- Latency SLO: p95 < 300ms for core assistant flows

Pricing qualification items we covered and items I still need from you:
- Target $/1M tokens you’re aiming for (you mentioned this is a key gate) — can you confirm a target range?
- Which model fidelity you expect (open-models vs higher-cost safety/quality models)
- Any contractual preference: hosted API vs dedicated/reserved capacity vs private deployment

Ballpark competitive benchmarks (for context, to help with target setting):
- OpenAI (higher-capacity chat models): roughly $100–$200 / 1M tokens depending on model and context length
- Anthropic (Claude-like): roughly $80–$150 / 1M tokens for chat workloads
- Other open-model hosts (Mistral/RedPajama hosted variants, quantized): roughly $20–$40 / 1M tokens depending on batching/quantization and infra efficiency

Our posture / options for Acme (summary):
- Hosted API (fastest ramp): simple per-token billing, typical entry pricing in the $40–$90 / 1M tokens range for open-models vs larger LM variants; good for POC and early production
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): predictable throughput + lower unit economics — we can reach mid/high $20s / 1M tokens at volume and multi-month commits
- Private (VPC / on-prem): custom pricing for enterprise — often the best at scale but requires procurement lead time

Attachments: I’ve attached a short workbook with a comparison matrix (redwood_pricing_vs_hosts.xlsx) and a token-volume estimate you can edit (token_volume_estimates.csv).

Next steps
1) Can you confirm your target $/1M tokens (range) and whether 100M/month is the right steady-state estimate?
2) If you confirm target, I’ll run a couple of pricing scenarios (hosted vs dedicated) and send a short proposal + sample unit economics by tomorrow.

Thanks — talk soon,
Vanessa

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T17:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: token volumes & target $/1M (Acme)

Thanks Vanessa — great summary. Confirming a few points from our side: 
- 100M/month is the right steady-state estimate for phase 1 (POC + initial rollout). We expect growth to ~300M+/month in 12–18 months if metrics look good.
- Embeddings at ~10M/month shared across search and rerank jobs.
- For POC we have a budget target of roughly $50k/month initially; our procurement people would like to see a target $/1M token that gets us within that budget at 100M tokens.

To be concrete: our internal target is roughly $25–$35 per 1M tokens for inference (open-model quality is fine for most flows). If we need higher safety/fidelity models we can look at a separate budget line.

Questions for your proposal:
- Can you show hosted pricing vs dedicated reserved pricing at 100M and 300M monthly volumes?
- Are there onboarding/ingress data costs for embeddings or hidden fees we should account for?

If you can get a scenario back tomorrow that maps to our $/1M target range and the $50k/month POC budget, that’ll help expedite procurement.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product — AI
Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com | (617) 555-3221
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: token volumes & target $/1M (Acme)

Alex — thanks, this is super helpful and aligns with what I expected. Attached is a short scenarios sheet; summary below (all numbers are illustrative and final quote will be in the proposal):

Scenario A — Hosted API (fastest ramp)
- Model: quantized open-model class (recommended for POC)
- Unit cost: $45 / 1M tokens
- 100M tokens => $4,500 / month (inference) + embeddings (10M) at $20 / 1M => $200 => total ~$4.7k / month

Scenario B — Dedicated Reserved (12mo commit)
- Model: same family but dedicated GPU pool + batching/kv caching
- Unit cost: $22 / 1M tokens (volume discount applied)
- 100M tokens => $2,200 / month + embeddings $150 => total ~$2.35k / month

Scenario C — Dedicated (higher volume, 300M)
- Tiered pricing to $18 / 1M tokens at 300M+ with commit
- 300M tokens => $5.4k / month

Competitor context (ballpark):
- OpenAI: $100–$200 / 1M tokens for higher-capacity chat models; fine for quality-critical flows but > our target
- Anthropic: $80–$150 / 1M tokens
- Hosted open-model vendors: $25–$40 / 1M tokens depending on quantization & infra efficiency

Takeaways and recommendations
- Given your $25–$35 / 1M target, the dedicated reserved path gets closest to target at scale. At 100M/month our dedicated example ($22 / 1M) is below your target range and well within the $50k POC budget.
- Hosted API is a low-friction way to validate; pricing is higher but still affordable for a short POC.

I’ve attached the workbook (redwood_pricing_vs_hosts.xlsx) with model assumptions and a per-token unit economics tab you can edit. No hidden ingress fees for embeddings — embeddings are charged per token; we’ll call out any data-transfer costs explicitly in the proposal if you choose private/on-prem.

Next steps
1) Confirm whether you want a hosted POC (fast) or we should price dedicated 12mo reserved (procurement lead time).
2) If dedicated, I can draft a term sheet with commit levels (100M, 300M) + initial discount cadence and send to procurement.

If helpful, I can also set up a quick call with Neha (solutions architect) to walk the tech + batching/kv cache impact on unit economics.

Thanks — I’ll stand by for which option you prefer.

—Vanessa

On attachments: redwood_pricing_vs_hosts.xlsx (pricing scenarios), token_volume_estimates.csv (editable)
